{{Short description|Category in category theory}}
In mathematics, especially [[category theory]], an '''accessible quasi-category''' is a [[quasi-category]] in which each object is an [[Ind-completion|ind-object]] on some small quasi-category. In particular, an accessible quasi-category is typically large (not small). The notion is a generalization of an earlier 1-category version of it, an [[accessible category]] introduced by Adámek and Rosický.<ref>Jiří Adámek, Jiří Rosický, Locally presentable and accessible categories, Cambridge University Press, (1994)</ref>

== Definition ==
An [[∞-category]] is called accessible or more precisely <math>\kappa</math>-accessible if it is equivalent to the ∞-category of <math>\kappa</math>-ind objects on some small ∞-category for some regular cardinal <math>\kappa</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|2009|loc=Definition 5.4.2.1.}}</ref>

== Facts ==
A small ∞-category is accessible if and only if it is [[idempotent-complete]].<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|2009|loc=Corollary 5.4.3.6.}}</ref>
